It’s like everyone is talking about me, or these news reports have secret messages just for me in them. Nothing sparks joy anymore – not even painting, which used to be my whole world. My dreams are another story; they've turned into these vivid, terrifying nightmares that leave me drained. I've been seeing figures in the periphery, shadows that coalesce into people, or sometimes vibrant, impossible colors swirling at the edges of my vision. It’s like they’re trying to show me something, a hidden truth. I have this feeling, deep down, that I’m meant for something extraordinary; I possess a unique understanding of the universe that others can't grasp. I try to explain it sometimes, but the words just escape me, coming out like a jumbled mess, and then it feels pointless to even try. D007-D015_h015.question_both:
Honestly, I'm not really sure why I’m here. My friends, or what's left of them, said I needed to talk to someone. Everything just feels… foggy, you know? It's been like this for about seven months.

The gigs used to be my life, a way to stay busy. Now, it's a huge effort to even get out of bed. The thought of picking up an order, dealing with people, it just feels impossible. I’ll sit there, staring at my phone, totally unable to make myself hit "accept." Lately, there are these women, everywhere I go, who I know are sending me signals, little smiles and looks that tell me they’re really into me. It's flattering, but also a bit overwhelming. And sometimes, usually at night, I see things, like shadows moving in the corner of my eye, or flickers of people that aren't actually there. It’s not terrifying, just… there.

When people ask me questions, my mind just goes off on tangents. I try to answer, but then one thought leads to another and I end up talking about something completely different. It's like my brain just can’t stay on track. And sometimes, it's hard to move, too. Like, if I'm sitting down, it takes a real effort to stand up, almost like my limbs are stiff. There's this heavy feeling, like I'm just a burden to everyone. I don't really see the point in anything anymore. I've even thought about just ending it all, pretty specific about how I'd do it, just to make it all stop.
D007-D015_h015.question_a:
It’s been, I guess, about seven months now that things have felt… off. I’m just so tired all the time, completely drained, and it’s a struggle to even get out of bed. My deliveries for the gig app have really suffered because of it. I just can't bring myself to care anymore, and when people ask me anything, it's like my brain moves in slow motion, trying to string words together. I feel worthless, like I'm just taking up space. Sometimes… sometimes I think about just driving my scooter off a bridge, or really concrete ways to just end it all.

But even before this feeling of being completely down, there were these other things happening. Like, about two weeks before I started feeling this heavy black cloud, I began seeing things—shadowy figures at the edge of my vision, almost like people, but they vanish when I look directly. And this woman, a customer from one of my regular routes, I just know she’s in love with me. She gives me these lingering looks, even tries to leave me bigger tips, because she can’t openly express her feelings. I know it seems strange, but it's undeniable. When all the sadness hit, those visuals and that certainty about her never went away, and they’ve continued even now, even on days the depression lessens a tiny bit. They’re always just… there. That’s why it feels different from just being depressed, you know?
D007-D015_h015.question_b:

There's this gnawing feeling that I'm just worthless, a waste of space. The thought of picking up a delivery, seeing people, it just feels like too much effort. I'm usually pretty quick-witted, but even talking feels like wading through mud sometimes, and it takes me forever to answer anything.

And then there's her. This woman, she’s a regular on my route from a few months back. I just know she’s in love with me. I see her sometimes, just a glimpse out the corner of my eye, even when I know she shouldn’t be there. It’s like she’s watching me, trying to send me a message through the streetlights. She’s definitely around, even when no one else sees her. It’s all so confusing. I once tried to explain it all to my buddy, but I ended up talking about the color of the sky and how it relates to bike gears, not what he asked. I know it sounds strange, but I feel like I'm made of clay sometimes; I just stay in whatever position I’m put in.

It all started around seven months ago, this whole depressive fog and the thoughts about her, the visions. It's only when I'm feeling this low, this deep, soul-crushing sadness, that these other things start happening. If I actually felt better, I know she wouldn't be there, and I wouldn't be seeing things. Sometimes I think about just ending it, I even have a spot picked out by the river. It feels like the only way out of this."
